chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm, when a man performs salat (prayer), in placing his knees on the ground before his hands.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as applying to a state of necessity in which a person is unable to meet the ground with his hands first, due to an ailment, illness, or something similar.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.لِعِلَّةٍ: due to an ailment or physical cause

ai.seo_question: When going into sajdah in salat (prayer), may a person place the knees on the ground before the hands?
ai.summary: This report addresses a ruling related to the manner of going down for sajdah in salat (prayer). Although it states there is no harm in placing the knees before the hands, the text explains that this is to be understood as applying in a case of necessity, such as illness or another impediment.
